text.S1: Near a great forest dwelt a poor woodcutter with his wife and his two children. The boy was called Hansel and the girl Gretel.
text.T1: Mupepi ne mpanga iikulu paikele shimapulanga na bakashi bakwe na abaana babibili. Umulumendo ishina Hansel elyo umukashana Gretel.
text.T2: Mupepi ne mpanga iikulu paikele shimapulanga na bakashi bakwe na abaana babibili. Umulumendo ishina Hansel elyo umukashana Gretel.

text.S1: He had little to bite and to break, and when great scarcity fell on the land, he could no longer procure daily bread. Now when he thought over this at night in his bed, and tossed about in his anxiety…
text.T1: Tabakwete ulupiya ulwingi iyoo. Elyo ba tontonkenye lintu icipoowe cawile pa ncende iyi, balefilwa nokushita umukate wa kulya cilabushiku, nokupilikita fye ubushiku bonse mu busanshi.
text.T2: Tabakwete ulupiya ulwingi iyoo. Elyo ba tontonkenye lintu icipoowe cawile pa ncende iyi, balefilwa nokushita umukate wa kulya cilabushiku, nokupilikita fye ubushiku bonse mu busanshi.

text.S1: he groaned and said to his wife, “What is to become of us? How are we to feed our poor children, when we no longer have anything even for ourselves?”
text.T1: Babulwime no kusosha abakashi ati, "Finshi fyala tucitikiila ifwe? Twalalisha shani abaana aba, elyo tatukwete nefyakuilisha fwebene?
text.T2: Babulwime no kusosha abakashi ati, "Finshi fyala tucitikila ifwe? Twalalisha shani abaana aba, elyo tatukwete nefyakuilisha fwebene?

text.S1: “I'll tell you what, husband,” answered the woman, “Early tomorrow morn- ing we will take the children out into the forest where it is the thickest. There we will light a fire for them, and give each of them one piece of bread, and then we will go to our work and leave them alone. They will not find the way home again, and we shall be rid of them.”
text.T1: " Lekeni myebe mwebalume bandi", fya aswiike abakashi, " Mailo luceelo-ceelo tukatwaala abaana mu mpanga mukati umwa tikamiisha, tukaba koseshe umulilo, nokuba pela ciila mwaana umukate, elyo tukaaye na ku ncito nokubasha beeka. Tabakalondoke ukubwela ku ng'anda nakabili, ninshi chapwa twapusuka kuli bena."
text.T2: " Lekeni myebe mwebalume bandi", efyaaswiike abakashi, " Mailo luceelo-ceelo tukatwaala abaana mu mpanga mukati umwa tikamiisha, tukaba koseshe umulilo, nokuba pela ciila mwaana umukate, elyo tukaaye na ku ncito nokubasha beeka. Tabakalondoke ukubwela ku ng'anda nakabili, ninshi capwa twapusuka kuli bena."

text.S1: “No, wife,” said the man, “I will not do that; how can I bear to leave my chil- dren alone in the forest? -the wild animals would soon come and tear them to pieces.”
text.T1: "Iyoo, mwebakashi bandi," efyasosele abalume, "Ine nshacite ico; kuti nakwanisha shani ukusha abaana bandi beeka mu mpanga?- ifinama kuti fya balya.
text.T2: "Iyoo, mwebakashi bandi," efyasosele abalume, "Ine nshacite ico; kuti nakwanisha shani ukusha abaana bandi beeka mu mpanga? Ifinama kuti fya balya.

text.S1: “O, you fool!” said she, “Then we must all four die of hunger. You may as well plane the planks for our coffins,” and she left him no peace until he con- sented. “But I feel very sorry for the poor children, all the same,” said the man.
text.T1: " Wecipumbu we!" efyasosele abakashi, "Lekeni kanshi bonse bane tukafwe ku nsala. Ambeni no kupopa imbokoshi shesu". Elyo balesosapofye mpanga abalume basumina. " Lelo naumfwa ububi ku baana"efyasosele bawishi.
text.T2: " Wecipumbu wee!" efyasosele abakashi, "Lekeni kanshi bonse bane tukafwe ku nsala. Ambeni no kupopa imbokoshi shesu". Elyo balesosapofye mpaka abalume basumina. " Lelo naumfwa ububi ku baana"efyasosele bawishi.

text.S1: The two children had also not been able to sleep for hunger, and had heard what their stepmother had said to their father. Gretel wept bitter tears, and said to Hansel, “Now all is over for us.” “Hush, Gretel,” said Hansel, “do not distress yourself, I will soon find a way to help us.”
text.T1: Abaana babili na bo tabaleele ku mulandu wa nsaala, elyo bali umfwa efyo banyiina balesosa kuli ba wishi. Gretel ali liila ifilaamba, elyo asosa kuli Hansel, "Nomba ifwe catupwiila". " Talala, Gretel," efyasosele Hansel, "wisakamana, nalafwaaya inshila iyakutwafwiilamo.
text.T2: Abaana babili nabo tabaleele ku mulandu wa nsala, elyo bali umfwa efyo banyiina balesosa kuli ba wishi. Gretel ali liila ifilaamba, elyo asosa kuli Hansel, "Nomba ifwe catupwiila". " Talala, Gretel," efyasosele Hansel, "wisakamana, nalafwaaya inshila iyakutwafwiilamo.

text.S1: And when the old folks had fallen asleep, he got up, put on his lit- tle coat, opened the door below, and crept outside. The moon shone brightly, and the white pebbles which lay in front of the house glittered like real silver pennies.
text.T1: Elyo abafyaashi basendeme, alibuuka, afwaala icikoti cakwe, aiswile iciibi kunshi icali kuntanshi ya ng'anda, elyo cashingulwike panse. Umweshi wa akiile pa mabwe tuutuayali pantanshi ya ng'anda kwati lupiya lwa silifele.
text.T2: Elyo abafyaashi basendeme, alibukile, afwaala icikoti cakwe, aiswile iciibi kunshi icali kuntanshi ya ng'anda, elyo cashingulwike panse. Umweshi wa akiile pa mabwe tuutu ayali pantanshi ya ng'anda kwati lupiya lwa silifele.

text.S1: Hansel stooped and put as many of them in the little pocket of his coat as he could possibly get in. Then he went back and said to Gretel, “Be  comforted, dear little sister, and sleep in peace, God will not forsake us,” and  he lay down again in his bed.
text.T1: Hansel afuukeme nokubiika amabwe ayengi mu matumba ya cikoti cakwe. Elyo abwelele nokusosa kuli Gretel, " Wisakamana wemutemwikwa, sendama.
text.T2: Hansel afuukeme nokubiika amabwe ayengi mu matumba ya cikoti cakwe. Elyo abwelele nokusosa kuli Gretel, " Wisakamana wemutemwikwa, sendama.

text.S1: When day dawned, but before the sun had risen, the woman came and awoke the two children, saying, “Get up, you sluggards! We are going into the forest to fetch wood.” She gave each a little piece of bread, and said, “There is something for your dinner, but do not eat it up before then, for you will get nothing else.”
text.T1: Lintu bwaciile uluceelo, Lintu akasuuba takala ima, banyiina baishile babusha abaana babili, ukuti, "Shibukeni, mwebanang'ani mwe! Tuleya mu mpanga mu ku fwaaya amapulanga". Ba pele cilamuntu umukate, nokusosa ati, eko fili ifyakulya fya cungulo, lelo mwilya fyonse apapene, pantu tapali fimbi.
text.T2: Lintu bwaceele uluceelo, ilyo akasuuba takala ima, banyiina baishile babusha abaana babili, ukuti, "Shibukeni, mwebanang'ani mwe! Tuleya mu mpanga mu ku fwaaya amapulanga". Ba pele cilamuntu umukate, nokusosa ati, eko fili ifyakulya fya cungulo, lelo mwilya fyonse apapene, pantu tapali fimbi.

text.S1: Gretel took the bread under her apron, as Hansel had the stones in his pocket. Then they all set out together on the way to the forest. When they had walked a short time, Hansel stood still and peeped back at the house, and did so again and again.
text.T1: Gretel abulile umukate no ku biika mu fyakufwaala fyakwe, elyo Hansel alikweete amabwe mu matumba. Elyo bonse baimine pamo ukuuya ku mpanga. Lintu baendele inshita iinono, Hansel aiminine no kulolesha kunuma ku ng'anda, nakabili elyo nakabili.
text.T2: Gretel abulile umukate no ku biika mu fyakufwaala fyakwe, elyo Hansel alikweete amabwe mu matumba. Elyo bonse baimine pamo ukuuya ku mpanga. Lintu baendele inshita iinono, Hansel aiminine no kulolesha kunuma ku ng'anda, nakabili elyo nakabili.

text.S1: His father said, “Hansel, what are you looking at there and staying behind for? Mind yourself, and do not forget how to use your legs.”
text.T1: Ba wishi batiile, "Hansel, finshi uleloleshya kunuma no ku shalila kunuma? Ichindiike, elyo akubomfya amakasa."
text.T2: Ba wishi batiile, "Hansel, finshi uleloleshya kunuma no ku shalila kunuma? Ichindiike, elyo wilaba ukubomfya amakasa."

text.S1: “Ah, father,” said Hansel, “I am looking at my little white cat, which is sitting up on the roof, and wants to say goodbye to me.” The wife said, “Fool, that is not your little cat, that is the morning sun which is shining on the chimneys.” Hansel, however, had not been looking back at the cat, but had been constantly throwing one of the white pebblestones out of his pocket on the road.
text.T1: "Ah, Taata", efyasosele Hansel, Ndeloleshya pushi wa buuta, uwikeele pa mutenge, alefwaaya ukundaaya". Abakashi batiile, "Wecipuba we, te pushi obe, ako kasuba akale ima. Hansel taleloleshya pushi, lelo aleposa amabwe ayabuuta ukufuuma mwitumba lyakwe mu musebo.
text.T2: "Ah, Taata", efyasosele Hansel, Ndelolesha pushi wa buuta, uwikeele pa mutenge, alefwaaya ukundaaya". Abakashi batiile, "Wecipuba we, te pushi obe, ako kasuba akale ima. Hansel taleloleshya pushi, lelo aleposa amabwe ayabuuta ukufuuma mwitumba lyakwe mu musebo.

text.S1: When they had reached the middle of the forest, the father said, “Now, chil- dren, pile up some wood, and I will light a fire that you may not be cold.” Hansel and Gretel gathered brushwood together, as high as a little hill.
text.T1: Lintu bafikiile pakati ka mpanga, ba wishi batiile, " Nomba, mwebaana, isusheni amapulanga, elyo nalamyasisha umulilo ukutiila mwi ingililwa ne mpepo. Hansel na Gretel balikolonganya amapulanga ayengi nga ulupili.
text.T2: Lintu bafikiile pakati ka mpanga, ba wishi batiile, " Nomba, mwebaana, isusheni amapulanga, elyo nalamyashisha umulilo ukutiila mwi ingililwa ne mpepo. Hansel na Gretel balikolongenye amapulanga ayengi nga ulupili.

text.S1: The brushwood was lighted, and when the flames were burning very high, the woman said, “Now, children, lay yourselves down by the fire and rest. We will go into the forest and cut some wood. When we have done, we will come back and fetch you away.”
text.T1: I mpanga yalipya, elyo umulilo wa kosele, banyiina batiile, "Nomba, mwebaana, sendameni ku mulilo mutushe. Twaaya ku mpanga mu ku putuula amapulanga elyo twalaisa misenda".
text.T2: lmpanga yalipya, elyo umulilo wa kosele, banyiina batiile, "Nomba, mwebaana, sendameni ku mulilo mutushe. Twaaya ku mpanga mu ku putuula amapulanga elyo twalaisa misenda".

text.S1: Hansel and Gretel sat by the fire, and when noon came, each ate a little piece of bread, and as they heard the strokes of the wood-axe they believed that their father was near. It was not, however, the axe, it was a branch which he had fastened to a withered tree which the wind was blowing backwards and forwards. And as they had been sitting such a long time, their eyes shut with fatigue, and they fell fast asleep. When at last they awoke, it was already dark night.
text.T1: Hansel na Gretel baikele ku mulilo, elyo akasuba kaisa, bonse batiile umukate wabo, elyo baleumfwa abalebomba mupepi, bamwene ukutiila mu na wishi abali mupepi. Lelo, tesembe bale umukate, cali cimuti na umwela wale puta. Elyo baikele panshita iitali, ameenso yashibete na ukunaaka, elyo basendeme. Elyo ba bukile, ninshi na bwiila na kale.
text.T2: Hansel na Gretel baikele ku mulilo, elyo akasuba kaisa, bonse baliile umukate wabo, elyo baleumfwa ukutetebuka kwa nkuni mupepi, bamwene ukutiila niba wishi abali mupepi. Lelo tesembe, cali cimuti na umwela wale puta. Elyo baikele panshita iitali, ameenso yashibete na ukunaaka, elyo basendeme. Elyo ba bukile, ninshi na bwiila na kale.

text.S1: Gretel began to cry and said, “How are we to get out of the forest now?” But Hansel comforted her and said, “Just wait a little, until the moon has risen, and then we will soon find the way.” And when the full moon had risen, Hansel took his little sister by the hand, and followed the pebbles which shone like newly-coined silver pieces, and showed them the way.
text.T1: Gretel atampile ukulila elyo asosele, "Lolelafye panono, mpanga umweshi wime, elyo twalasuuka tu fwaaye inshila". Lintu umweshi waimine, Hansel asendele umwaice wakwe pakuboko, nokukonka amabwe ayale beeka nga ulupiya lwa silifele nokubalanga inshila.
text.T2: Gretel atampile ukulila elyo asosele, "Lolelafye panono, mpaka umweshi wime, elyo twalasuka tu fwaaye inshila". Lintu umweshi waimine, Hansel asendele umwaice wakwe pakuboko, nokukonka amabwe ayale beeka nga ulupiya lwa silifele nokubalanga inshila.

text.S1: They walked the whole night long, and by break of day came once more to their father's house. They knocked at the door, and when the woman opened it and saw that it was Hansel and Gretel, she said, “You naughty children, why have you slept so long in the forest? We thought you were never coming back at all!”
text.T1: Baendele ubushiku bonse, elyo bwacile ulucelo balifiika ku ng'anda kuli ba wishi ku ng'anda. Balikonkonsha ku ciibi, elyo banyiina baiswile iciibi, bamona Hansel na Gretel, batiile, " Mwe baana tamumfwa mwacisendaminina mu mpanga? Twacimona kwati na mwakabwele ku ng'anda!"
text.T2: Baendele ubushiku bonse, elyo bwacile ulucelo balifikile kuli ba wishi ku ng'anda. Balikonkonsha ku ciibi, elyo banyiina baiswile iciibi, bamona Hansel na Gretel, batiile, " Mwe baana tamumfwa mwacisendaminina mu mpanga? Twacitontonkanya kwati tamwakabwele ku ng'anda!"

text.S1: The father, however, rejoiced, for it had cut him to the heart to leave them behind alone. Not long afterwards, there was once more great scarcity in all parts, and the children heard their mother saying at night to their father, “Everything is eaten again, we have one half loaf left, and after that there is no more. The children must go. We will take them farther into the wood, so that they will not find their way out again; there is no other means of saving ourselves!”
text.T1: Ba wishi, bali umfwa bwino pantu cali beekata ku mutima ukubasha beeka abaana mu mpanga. Nakabili insaala yawiile pancende yabo, baumfwiile ba nyiina ubushiku bale eba ba wishi ukutiila. "Ifyakulya fyonse fya pwa pang'anda. Umukate ushelefye uunono, ninshi wapwa. Ifyakulisha abaana tapali. Kabaleeya. Tukabatwalefye mukati ukutaali nakabili mu mpanga, ukutiila bekalondooka nakabili; tapalipo ne nshila iya kuipususishamo.
text.T2: Ba wishi, bali umfwa bwino pantu cali beekata ku mutima ukubasha beeka abaana mu mpanga. Nakabili insaala yawiile pancende yabo, baumfwiile ba nyiina ubushiku bale eba ba wishi ukutiila. "Ifyakulya fyonse fya pwa pang'anda. Umukate ushelefye uunono, ninshi wapwa. Ifyakulisha abaana tapali. Kabaleeya. Tukabatwalefye mukati ukutaali nakabili mu mpanga, ukutiila bekalondoka nakabili; tapalipo ne nshila iya kuipususishamo.

text.S1: The man's heart was heavy, and he thought, “It would be better for you to share the last mouthful with your children.” The woman, however, would listen to nothing that he had to say, but scolded and reproached him. He who says what must say what, likewise, and as he had yielded the first time, he had to do so a second time also.
text.T1: Abalume, umutima wafina, batontonkenye, lelo abakashi tabalefyumfwa nakalya, elyo babakalipile. Basuuka basumina nga efyo cali pakwamba.
text.T2: Abalume, umutima wafina, batontonkanya, lelo abakashi tabalefyumfwa nakalya, elyo babakalipile. Basuuka basumina nga efyo cali pakubala.

text.S1: The children were, however, still awake and had heard the conversation. When the old folks were asleep, Hansel again got up, and wanted to go out and pick up pebbles as he had done before, but the woman had locked the door, and Hansel could not get out. Nevertheless, he comforted his little sister, and said, “Do not cry, Gretel, go to sleep quietly, the good God will help us.”
text.T1: Abaana tabasendeme, iyoo, elyo l, Hansel na kabili ali buuka, elyo alefwaaya ukuuya toola amabwe nakabili, lelo banyiina bali koma iciibi. Lelo, aebele umwaice wakwe ukutiila "Wisakamana iyoo, leka ukulila, Lesa alatwafwa.
text.T2: Abaana tabasendeme, iyoo, elyo Hansel na kabili abuuka, elyo alefwaaya ukuuya toola amabwe nakabili, lelo banyiina bali koma iciibi. Lelo, aebele umwaice wakwe ukutiila "Wisakamana iyoo, leka ukulila, Lesa alatwafwa.

text.S1: Early in the morning came the woman, and took the children out of their beds. Their bit of bread was given to them, but it was still smaller than the time before. On the way into the forest Hansel crumbled his in his pocket, and often stood still and threw a morsel on the ground. “Hansel, why do you stop and look round?” said the father, “go on.”
text.T1: Uluceelo-celo banyiina baishile mu ku na buusha, no ku na fumya mu busanshi. Umukate wabo wapelwe kuli bena, lelo walicepele saana. Munshila pa kuuya ku mpanga Hansel alishonaula umukate wakwe mu matumba, elyo nokula imanina nokupoosa panshi. " Hansel, cinshi ule imanina nokulolesha loleshya? Basosele ba wishi, "Akwenda".
text.T2: Uluceelo-celo banyiina baishile mukuba buusha, no kuba fumya mu busanshi. Umukate wabo wapelwe kuli bena, lelo walicepele saana. Munshila pa kuuya ku mpanga Hansel alishonaula umukate wakwe mu matumba, elyo nokula imanina nokupoosa panshi. " Hansel, cinshi ule imanina nokulolesha loleshya? Efyasosele ba wishi, "Akwenda".

text.S1: “I am looking back at my little pigeon which is sitting on the roof, and wants to say goodbye to me,"answered Hansel.
text.T1: " Ndeloleshya akoni kandi akekele pa mutenge, elyo nde ka laya," fya aswiike Hansel.
text.T2: " Ndeloleshya akoni kandi akekele pa mutenge, elyo nde ka laya," efyaaswiike Hansel.

text.S1: “Simpleton!” said the woman, “that is not your little pigeon, that is the morning sun that is shining on the chimney.” Hansel, however, little by little, threw all the crumbs on the path.
text.T1: "Wekaice we!" Fyasosele banyiina, " te koni kobe kalya iyoo, kalya kasuba akekele pamutenge ". Hansel ena ta nakiile aleposafye panono panono, aposele munshila yonse ubufungau bwa mukate.
text.T2: "Wekaice we!" Fyasosele banyiina, " te koni kobe kalya iyoo, kalya kasuba akekele pamutenge ". Hansel ena ta nakiile aleposafye panono panono, aposele munshila yonse ubufungau bwa mukate.

text.S1: The woman led the children still deeper into the forest, where they had never  in their lives been before. Then a great fire was again made, and the mother  said, “Just sit there, you children, and when you are tired you may sleep a little;  we are going into the forest to cut wood, and in the evening when we are done,  we will come and fetch you away.”
text.T1: Abanakashi nakabili banyiina batwele mukati nakabili mwa mpanga eko tabatalile ukufiika nangula ukumonapo, elyo nga mwa nakabili kuti mwa sendama, icungulo nga twapwisha kuti twaisa misenda.
text.T2: Abanakashi, kabili banyiina batwele abaana mukati ka mpanga eko tabatalile ukufiika nangula ukumonapo, elyo nga mwanaka kuti mwa sendama, icungulo nga twapwisha kuti twaisa misenda.

text.S1: When it was noon, Gretel shared her piece of bread with Hansel, who had scattered his by the way. Then they fell asleep and evening came and went, but no one came to the poor children. They did not awake until it was dark night, and Hansel comforted his little sister and said, “Just wait, Gretel I, until the moon rises, and then we shall see the crumbs of bread which I have strewn about, they will show us our way home again.” When the moon came they set out, but they found no crumbs...
text.T1: Elyo akasuba kali pakati, Gretel aakene umukate wakwe nakabili ndumw wakwe Hansel uwa poseele umukate wakwe mu nshila pa kwisa. Elyo bonse babili basendeme utuulo, lelo tapali abaishile mu kuba senda. Babukile munshila na pa fita, Hansel aebele akaice kakwe ukutiila "Wisakamana,Lolela Gretel, twalamona umukate nacilaposa munshila. Lintu umweshi waimine, ubufungau bwa mukate tapali…
text.T2: Elyo akasuba kali pakati, Gretel aakenye umukate wakwe na ndume yakwe Hansel uwa poseele umukate wakwe mu nshila pa kwisa. Elyo bonse babili basendeme utuulo, lelo tapali abaishile mu kuba senda. Babukile munshila napa fiita, Hansel aebele akaice kakwe ukutiila "Wisakamana, lolela Gretel, twalamona umukate nacilaposa munshila. Lintu umweshi waimine, ubufungau bwa mukate tapali...

text.S1: For the many thousands of birds which fly about in the woods and fields had picked them all up. Hansel said to Gretel, “We shall soon find the way,” but they did not find it. They walked the whole night and all the next day too from morning till evening, but they did not get out of the forest, and were very hungry, for they had nothing to eat but two or three berries, which grew on the ground. And as they were so weary that their legs would carry them no longer, they lay down beneath a tree and fell asleep.
text.T1: Utoni twa mu muulu twalilya umukate. Hansel atiile kuli Gretel," Twalaisanga inshila", Lelo, tabaisangile. Balienda, ubushiku bwaila, uluceelo bwaca caba ne cungulo, lelo taba fumine mu mpanga, elyo bali ne nsaala, balilefya tubili nangula tutatu utwamumpanga utwakulya twalekuula panshi. Amoolu nayo yali naka, baikele munshi ya cimuti elyo basendama.
text.T2: Utoni twa mu muulu twalilya umukate. Hansel atiile kuli Gretel," Twalaisanga inshila", Lelo, tabaisangile. Balienda, ubushiku bwaila, uluceelo bwaca caba ne cungulo, lelo taba fumine mu mpanga, elyo bali ne nsaala, balilefye amalubeni yabili nangula yatatu ayaamumpanga ayalekulila panshi. Amoolu nayo yali naka, baikele munshi ya cimuti elyo basendama.

text.S1: It was now three mornings since they had left their father's house. They began to walk again, but they always got deeper into the forest, and if help did not come soon, they would die of hunger and weariness. When it was midday, they saw a beautiful snow-white bird sitting on a bough, which sang so delightfully that they stood still and listened to it. And when it had finished its song, it spread its wings and flew away before them, and they followed it until they reached a little house, on the roof of which it alighted; and when they came quite up to the little house they saw that it was built of bread and covered with cakes, but that the windows were of clear sugar.
text.T1: Bwali bushiku bwa citatu, epo bafumine ku ng'anda ya ba wishi. Batampile ukwenda nakabili, lelo bale ya mukati na nkati ya mpanga, elyo nga tapali abeshile mu ku bafwilisha, balipa kufwa fye. Akasuba bamwene akoni akabuuta tuutu, nakekala pa cimuti, kale imba bwino saana, baikele balakomfwa. Lintu kapwiile ulwimbo, kapupuka kaaya, elyo bakakonkele mpanga bafiika ku ng'anda mu mpanga. Lintu baikele mupepi ba mwene ukutiila ya pangilwe ba umukate, tu mpukunya matobo,elyo ama windo ba pangile na shuuka.

text.S1: “We will set to work on  that,” said Hansel, “and have a good meal. I will eat a bit of the roof, and you,  Gretel, can eat some of the window, it will taste sweet.” Hansel reached up  above, and broke off a little of the roof to try how it tasted, and Gretel leaned  against the window and nibbled at the panes. Then a soft voice cried from the room…

text.S1: “Nibble, nibble, gnaw,  Who is nibbling at my little house?” The children answered, “The wind, the wind,  The heaven-born wind,” and went on eating without disturbing themselves. Hansel, who thought the  roof tasted very nice, tore down a great piece of it, and Gretel pushed out the  whole of one round windowpane, sat down, and enjoyed herself with it.

text.S1: Sud- denly the door opened, and a very, very old woman, who supported herself on crutches, came creeping out. Hansel and Gretel were so terribly frightened that they let fall what they had in their hands. The old woman, however, nodded her head, and said, “Oh, you dear children, who has brought you here? Do come in, and stay with me. No harm shall happen to you.” She took them both by the hand, and led them into her little house. Then good food was set before them, milk and pancakes, with sugar, apples, and nuts. Afterwards two pretty little beds were covered with clean white linen, and Hansel and Gretel lay down in them, and thought they were in heaven.
text.T1: Iciibi cali iswiike, elyo ka nakulu, akale bomfya inkonto, bafumiine. Hansel na Gretel bali umfwa umwenso apakalamba, elyo baponeshe nefyali mu maboko yabo. Akakote kena kali pukunya umutwe nokusosa, " Iye, mwe baana, cinshi ca mileta ku no? Ingileni, ikaleni na ine. Tapali ifika micena. Babasendele pa maboko no ku bengisha mu ka yanda kabo. Elyo babapeela ifyakulya ifisuuma, impukunya matobo, imbalala, ifyalowa-lowa fyonse ifyakulya na umukaka. Elyo babapela na apakusendama pabili, nensala ishipya. Elyo Hansel na Gretel basendeme ukumona kwati na na fiika ku muulu.

text.S1: The old woman had only pretended to be so kind; she was in reality wicked . When a child fell into her power, she killed it,  cooked and ate it, and that was a feast day with her. Witches have red eyes, and  cannot see far, but they have a keen scent like the beasts, and are aware when  human beings draw near. When Hansel and Gretel came into her neighborhood, she laughed maliciously, and said mockingly, “I have them, they  shall not escape me again!”
text.T1: Akakote kalebepafye ukutiila kali na bwino; alini ndoshi mu cine. Umwaana na awiila mu maaka yabo, aleipaya, baipika, no kulya abaana. Indoshi, shakwete amenso aya mulopa-mulopa, elyo taba mona apatali, lelo balanunshya nefili apatali nokwishiba abantu nga bapalama. Elyo Hansel na Gretel baishile mupepi bali umfwa bwino no kuseka uluseko, nokusosa na abaana, "Abaana bandi, tabakamfyuuke iyoo!"

text.S1: Early in the morning before the children were awake, she was already up,  and when she saw both of them sleeping and looking so pretty, with their  plump red cheeks, she muttered to herself, “That will be a dainty mouthful!”  Then she seized Hansel with her shriveled hand, carried him into a little stable, and shut him in with a grated door. He might scream as he liked, that was  of no use. Then she went to Gretel, shook her till she awoke, and cried, “Get  up, lazy thing, fetch some water, and cook something good for your brother,  he is in the stable outside, and is to be made fat. When he is fat, I will eat him.”

text.S1: And now the best food was cooked for poor Hansel, but Gretel got nothing but crab shells. Every morning the woman crept to the little stable, and cried, “Hansel, stretch out your finger that I may feel if you will soon be fat.” Hansel, however, stretched out a little bone to her, and the old woman, who had dim eyes, could not see it, and thought it was Hansel's finger, and was astonished that there was no way of fattening him.

text.S1: “Just keep your noise to yourself,” said the old woman, “all that won't help you at all.” Early in the morning, Gretel had to go out and hang up the cauldron with the water, and light the fire. “We will bake first,” said the old woman. “I have al- ready heated the oven, and kneaded the dough.” She pushed poor Gretel out to the oven, from which flames of fire were already darting. “Creep in,” said the witch, “and see if it is properly heated, so that we can shut the bread in.” And once Gretel was inside, she intended to shut the oven and let her bake in it, and then she would eat her, too.

Then Gretel  gave her a push that drove her far into it, and shut the iron door, and fastened  the bolt. Oh! Then she began to howl quite terribly, but Gretel ran away, and the godless witch was miserably burnt to death.

And as they had no longer any need to fear her, they went into the witch's house, and in every corner, there stood chests full of pearls and jewels.

text.S1: The duck came to them, and Hansel seated himself on its back, and told his sister to sit by him. “No,” replied Gretel, “that will be too heavy for the little duck; she shall take us across, one after the other.” The good little duck did so, and when they were safely across and had walked for a short time, the forest seemed to be more and more familiar to them, and at length they saw from afar their father's house. Then they began to run, rushed into the parlor, and threw themselves into their father's arms. The man had not known one happy hour since he had left the children in the forest; the woman, however, was dead. Gretel emptied her pinafore until pearls and precious stones ran about the room, and Hansel threw one handful after another out of his pocket to add to them. Then all anxiety was at an end, and they lived together in perfect happiness.
